key: Maximum Entropy + Optimal Control + Tensor Decomposition

concepts.name: Maximum Entropy
concepts.short_description: Least biased inference consistent with constraints; Jaynes' principle, exponential families, log-linear models.

concepts.name: Optimal Control
concepts.short_description: Minimizing cost over trajectories; Pontryagin's principle, Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman, LQR.

concepts.name: Tensor Decomposition
concepts.short_description: Factoring multi-dimensional arrays into simpler components; CP, Tucker, and tensor train formats.

hypotheses.statement: The exponential (maximum-entropy) transform of a cost-to-go is a rank-changing map: under KL-regularized optimal control the desirability exp(-V/lambda) may be far lower tensor-rank than V itself, so maximum entropy is what makes optimal control tensor-compressible, and temperature is a knob on representational complexity.

Tensor rank is a control budget: an agent may only deploy policies whose joint action (or state-action) tensor has CP/nonnegative rank at most R, and maximum entropy fills all freedom left by that budget; intelligence is then the trade between rank spent and cost reduced.

Maximum entropy's unsolved choice of which constraints to impose is answered by control: the agent should constrain only the moments aligned with factors of its cost-to-go tensor and stay maximally ignorant elsewhere, so its world model is shaped by what it must control, not by what it must predict.

Bond dimension is required memory: a maximum-entropy distribution over trajectories subject to control-relevant constraints is a tensor train over time, and its bond dimension at each time cut counts how much memory any controller realizing it must carry.

Temperature drives rank transitions: as the entropy weight falls, the Gibbs policy of a coupled multi-actuator cost passes from product (rank 1) through a high-rank intermediate regime to a mixture of ground states, so there is a characteristic temperature where coordination is most representationally expensive.

Multipliers and costates are the same kind of object (prices of constraints); stacking them over time, state dimension and constraint index gives a price tensor whose low-rank structure would reveal a small number of latent 'concerns' that the controller actually trades off.

Rank as an evolvable trait: in a population of controllers represented as sums of rank-1 components, mutation adds, deletes, or splits components and selection acts on entropy-regularized cost, so effective rank is a heritable complexity measure whose equilibrium value is set by the task, not by a penalty.

Desirability-rank law: for KL-regularized control on a product state space with product passive dynamics, the desirability tensor z = exp(-V/lambda) has TT rank no larger than, and often much smaller than, V; rank(z) tracks the rank of the non-additive (coupling) part of the state cost rather than the number of state factors.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: the exponential transform that turns additive cost into multiplicative weight and linearizes the Bellman equation
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the cost-to-go V and the backward recursion that builds it
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: the rank observable and the TT-SVD that measures it

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: V would be computed directly; additive costs give TT rank 2 for V but no multiplicative collapse to rank 1
knockouts.Optimal Control: no value/desirability object exists; only a static tensor
knockouts.Tensor Decomposition: the claim reduces to 'linear Bellman is easier', with no complexity observable

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Any monotone smoothing of V (e.g. softmin) reduces numerical rank because it flattens dynamic range, not because of the exponential's multiplicative structure.

hypotheses.statement: Rank-budgeted maximum-entropy policy: the organism's joint action distribution is a mixture of R product distributions (nonnegative CP rank R); within that budget it minimizes expected cost minus lambda times entropy. The free-energy gap versus R has a knee at the number of coordination modes the cost actually demands.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: entropy term that makes the optimum a Gibbs distribution and gives a well-defined gap
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the cost over joint actions being minimized
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: the rank budget and mixture-of-products representation

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: policy collapses to argmin (rank = number of ties); no knee from temperature
knockouts.Optimal Control: no cost, the maxent optimum is uniform and rank 1 for every R
knockouts.Tensor Decomposition: an unrestricted policy with no complexity axis

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Parameter-count-limited policy with a generic capacity curve; the knee is just the point of diminishing returns of any capacity.

hypotheses.statement: Temperature-driven rank transition: the nonnegative rank needed to approximate the Gibbs policy of a coupled cost to fixed KL tolerance is non-monotone in inverse temperature beta: 1 at high temperature, peaking at an intermediate beta, and settling at the number of ground states at low temperature.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: temperature parameter and the Gibbs family
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the cost whose minima define the low-temperature limit
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: the rank needed as the order parameter

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: no temperature axis; only the argmin set exists
knockouts.Optimal Control: no cost structure; rank of the uniform distribution is 1 always
knockouts.Tensor Decomposition: no order parameter to observe the transition

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Numerical rank of any sharpening family grows then shrinks as it interpolates between uniform and a point mass; nothing specific to coordination.

questions.what_is_selected: the rank-minimal approximation at each beta
questions.what_can_learn: an agent could learn which beta it can afford
questions.what_can_transfer: the beta of peak rank as a signature of the coupling graph

hypotheses.statement: Control-relevant constraint selection: a maximum-entropy world model constrains only the moments lying in the span of the leading Tucker factors of the stacked desirability tensor over past goals; it is maximally ignorant elsewhere. It should transfer to new goals sharing those factors and fail on goals built from orthogonal factors, more sharply than a prediction-relevant model.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: the principle that everything not constrained is left at maximum ignorance
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the goals, desirability functions, and regret used to judge the model
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: the Tucker factors that define which moments are constrained

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: model would be arbitrary within the subspace; no principled ignorance off-subspace
knockouts.Optimal Control: factors would be chosen for prediction; the crossover disappears
knockouts.Tensor Decomposition: constraints would be chosen by an unstructured feature search; no shared-factor transfer

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Standard multi-task representation learning (shared low-rank subspace of value functions) with no maximum-entropy content.

hypotheses.statement: Price tensor: stacking constraint multipliers (maximum entropy) and costates (Pontryagin) over time, state coordinate and constraint index yields a tensor whose Tucker core size counts the independent constraint 'concerns' the controller trades off, which can be smaller than the number of active constraints.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: multipliers as prices of moment constraints
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: costates as prices of dynamics constraints
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: the Tucker core as the count of latent concerns

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: only costates remain; the tensor loses its constraint axis
knockouts.Optimal Control: only static multipliers; no time axis
knockouts.Tensor Decomposition: a list of multipliers with no latent-structure measure

questions.what_can_transfer: price factors across problems with shared constraints
questions.distinguishing_observable: core size lower than active-constraint count, beyond what the constraint Jacobian rank predicts

hypotheses.statement: Entropy bounds degeneracy: near a border-rank configuration, CP-factored controllers fitted by least squares develop diverging, mutually cancelling components; representing the policy as a maximum-entropy log-linear model whose natural parameters are CP-factored, and penalizing policy KL from passive dynamics, bounds component norms and removes the divergence.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: KL/entropy regularization that bounds how extreme any component can be
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the cost that pulls the fit toward the degenerate target
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: border rank and the CP degeneracy phenomenon itself

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Weight decay (L2 on factors) prevents divergence equally well.

questions.what_exists: CP-factored natural parameters, a degenerate target
questions.what_can_transfer: a bounded fit transfers to perturbed targets more smoothly
questions.distinguishing_observable: component-norm growth with KL regularization versus L2 matched on the same achieved fit error

hypotheses.statement: Bond dimension equals controller memory: the maximum-entropy trajectory distribution under k soft interval constraints is a TT over time whose bond dimension at each cut is bounded by the number of distinct partial sufficient-statistic values; any finite-state controller reproducing it needs at least that many memory states, whereas non-additive constraints break the bound.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: the exponential-family trajectory law with additive sufficient statistics
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the controller that must realize the distribution with finite memory

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: an arbitrary trajectory distribution has no sufficient-statistic bound
knockouts.Optimal Control: no controller; statement becomes pure automata theory

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Finite-automaton state counting (Myhill-Nerode classes) gives the same number without tensors or entropy.

questions.what_exists: trajectories, soft constraints, a TT over time
questions.what_can_transfer: memory machines across constraint sets sharing features
questions.distinguishing_observable: bond dimension versus distinct-conditional-future count under additive and non-additive constraints

hypotheses.statement: Rank-1 modules: each CP component is a module that runs its own product (independent-actuator) maximum-entropy policy; modules interact only by being mixed; the number of modules a task sustains equals the coupling rank of its cost at the operating temperature. Three-way dependency is moderate: this is close to a mixture-of-products with a cost.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: within-module independence (product = maximum entropy given marginals)
concept_contributions.Optimal Control: the shared cost that allocates weight between modules

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: modules would be arbitrary joint policies; count uninterpretable
knockouts.Optimal Control: no reason for modules to differ

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Mixture of experts with a gating prior; module count set by capacity.

questions.what_can_transfer: modules between tasks with a shared coordination mode
questions.distinguishing_observable: number of surviving modules versus ground-state count and versus shuffled-cost null

hypotheses.statement: ALS as soft best response: one ALS sweep over CP factors of a joint policy equals each actuator computing a maximum-entropy (softmin) best response to the others' current marginals; the fixed points are quantal-response-type equilibria and rank is the number of coexisting equilibria a single policy can hold.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: softmin replaces argmin in each block update

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: hard best response; cycling and non-smoothness

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Block-coordinate descent / fictitious play with smoothing; the tensor language adds nothing.

questions.distinguishing_observable: number of distinct fixed points reached from random starts versus fitted rank

hypotheses.statement: Rank mutation: controllers are genomes of rank-1 components; mutations add a component, delete one, split one into two perturbed copies, or merge two; selection is on negative free energy (cost minus lambda entropy). Without any explicit complexity penalty, effective rank (exp of mixture-weight entropy after merging near-duplicates) converges to the task's required rank.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: the entropy term that gives a finite-temperature target
concept_contributions.Tensor Decomposition: the component genome and rank-changing operators

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: target is argmin; effective rank equals tie count, weaker test
knockouts.Tensor Decomposition: no genome structure; ordinary parameter evolution

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Any evolution with redundancy: surplus components are neutral and wander, and effective-rank convergence reflects merging, not selection.

questions.what_is_selected: genomes with higher negative free energy
questions.what_can_transfer: components between lineages facing different temperatures
questions.distinguishing_observable: evolved effective rank versus W2's required rank, and versus shuffled-cost populations

hypotheses.statement: Gauge-neutral drift: the Tucker/TT gauge freedom of a factored controller is a neutral space; drift along it changes nothing about cost or entropy but changes which single-factor mutations are beneficial, so gauge drift could set evolvability. Three-way dependency is weak: maximum entropy only supplies the fitness.

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: fitness still exists with plain cost; little is lost

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Neutral networks in any redundant parameterization do the same.

questions.distinguishing_observable: fraction of beneficial mutations as a function of gauge after drift versus canonical gauge

hypotheses.statement: Distribution steering as rank-1 factorization in time: steering a population from an initial to a target set of moments with minimal KL from passive dynamics yields a trajectory law that factorizes as forward potential times backward potential; the TT bond dimension across the midpoint is 1 per constraint pair and grows only with intermediate constraints.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: This is plausibly an already-known bridge/linearly solvable control result restated; the tensor view may add only a counting convention.

questions.what_can_transfer: potentials between tasks sharing a boundary
questions.distinguishing_observable: bond dimension versus number of intermediate constraints

hypotheses.statement: Multi-goal compression pressure: an agent that must serve many goals under a per-goal entropy (KL) budget is pressured toward sharing low-rank factors across the goal-by-state desirability tensor; the achieved goal-mode rank falls as the KL budget tightens.

concept_contributions.Maximum Entropy: the KL budget that prices deviation from passive behaviour

knockouts.Maximum Entropy: no budget; no pressure to share

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: Multi-task learning under capacity limits shares representations for generic reasons.

questions.what_exists: an agent, a family of goals
questions.what_is_selected: shared factors that help many goals
questions.distinguishing_observable: goal-mode rank as a function of KL budget at matched parameter count

hypotheses.statement: Rank deficit as control price: the minimal KL a controller must pay to reach a joint-state target equals the sum over CP components of per-component log-partition differences plus an interaction term that vanishes iff the target's coupling rank is 1. Speculative identity; three-way dependency is strong but the statement may be false for most targets.
hypotheses.simpler_alternative: KL between product and joint is just multi-information; rank adds nothing beyond total correlation.

questions.what_exists: passive product dynamics and a joint target
questions.distinguishing_observable: interaction term versus total correlation of the target at fixed rank

hypotheses.statement: Coarse-to-fine by rank: a controller develops by first solving the rank-1 (independent-factor) maximum-entropy approximation at high temperature, then annealing temperature and adding components only when the free-energy gap exceeds a threshold; developmental order of components follows the coupling strength order.

concept_contributions.Optimal Control: cost that orders components by value

hypotheses.simpler_alternative: A curriculum from easy to hard produces the same ordering.

questions.what_exists: a controller and a temperature schedule
questions.distinguishing_observable: order of acquired components versus coupling strengths, compared with random-order addition

hypotheses.statement: W4 probe round 1: NULL. Attempt 1 was INSTRUMENT_FAIL (positive control 0/10: my goal construction put the cost offset outside the K=2 shared span); one repair moved the constant into the shared span, all else unchanged. Attempt 2: rule (a) HOSVD beats rule (b) prediction subspace strongly on in-span goals (median in-span ratio b/a = 24.3, 10/10 seeds >= 2) but shows no meaningful reversal on orthogonal goals (median off-span ratio a/b = 1.022, needed >= 1.2), so 0/10 seeds meet the joint criterion: NULL. The formal failure criterion is not met (off-span ratio > 1 in 10/10 seeds, range 1.004-1.079), so this is a fails-to-reach-success NULL, not a failure-criterion kill. Null twin loses the in-span advantage (median 0.91); random subspace is ~20x worse everywhere. Both (a) and (b) have ~0.006 relative regret on orthogonal goals.

lenses.name: Exponential-rank spectrometer
lenses.rationale: M1/M3 claim the maxent exponential changes tensor complexity; measure it directly and against matched non-exponential transforms.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: full value tensor V and desirability z over a product state space
lenses.transformation: TT-SVD of V, of exp(-V/lambda), and of rank-matched monotone controls (tanh, rank-preserving quantile maps) at each lambda
observables: TT bond dimensions at relative Frobenius tolerance 1e-6 and 1e-3
lenses.nullExpectation: on entry-shuffled costs bond(z) and bond(V) both saturate near full rank
failureModes: exp saturates to near-constant at large lambda, trivially rank 1
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates the multiplicative structure of the maxent transform from generic dynamic-range compression

lenses.name: Free-energy knee finder
lenses.rationale: M2/M8/M10 predict a characteristic rank; find the knee of the free-energy-gap-versus-rank curve.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: joint action cost tensor and mixture-of-products policies at ranks 1..Rmax
lenses.transformation: fit each rank by EM to the Gibbs target, record KL gap, detect knee by max second difference of log gap
observables: R* = smallest R with KL gap < 0.01 nats
predictedSignals: R* equals ground-state count at low temperature
lenses.nullExpectation: shuffled-cost R*(beta) rises smoothly and exceeds structured R* at intermediate beta
failureModes: EM local optima understate achievable fit
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: measures nonnegative (mixture) rank, the operationally relevant rank for policies, which L1's signed TT rank does not

lenses.name: Cancellation seismograph
lenses.rationale: M6 is about divergent cancelling components; measure cancellation directly.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: CP factor sets over a fitting trajectory
lenses.transformation: compute cancellation ratio (sum of component norms / norm of reconstructed tensor) per iteration
predictedSignals: unbounded growth under least squares near border rank; bounded under KL regularization
lenses.nullExpectation: L2 penalty matched on final fit error bounds norms equally
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: sees ill-posedness of the representation, not its size

lenses.name: Transfer crossover plot
lenses.rationale: M4/M13 predict that control-shaped models win in-span and lose off-span; a crossover is a sharper signature than a mean advantage.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: regret of subspace-restricted linear-Bellman solutions on held-out goals
lenses.transformation: group test goals into in-span and orthogonal; compute median regret ratio per subspace-selection rule
observables: median regret per rule per group
lenses.nullExpectation: with fiber-permuted training desirabilities the in-span advantage vanishes
failureModes: orthogonal goals accidentally aligned with passive-dynamics eigenvectors
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: tests maxent-as-ignorance behaviourally rather than representationally

lenses.name: Cut-memory ledger
lenses.rationale: M7/M12 equate TT bond dimension over time with memory; count both independently.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: trajectory distribution tensor over T binary steps
lenses.transformation: TT-SVD across time cuts; separately count distinct normalized conditional futures and distinct partial sufficient statistics
predictedSignals: bond = statistic count under additive constraints; bond > statistic count under non-additive constraints
lenses.nullExpectation: bond dimension equals min of unfolding sizes for random distributions
failureModes: identity is mathematically forced (no empirical content)
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: converts representation size into a controller-memory requirement

lenses.name: Rank genealogy
lenses.rationale: M10/M11/M15 are about how rank arises in lineages; track components as heritable units.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: population genomes of rank-1 components with parent pointers
lenses.transformation: track effective rank per lineage, component ages, and merge/split events over generations
predictedSignals: effective rank converges to required rank from L2
lenses.nullExpectation: effective rank drifts upward neutrally when components cost nothing
failureModes: near-duplicate merge threshold decides the result
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: adds heritability/history to a quantity other lenses see only at a snapshot

experiments.hypothesis: Under KL-regularized control on a product space, max TT rank of desirability z is lower than that of V, and tracks the planted coupling rank.
experiments.mechanism: Linear Bellman (z = exp(-q/lambda) * P z, finite horizon) on product passive dynamics, compared with the value V = -lambda log z.
experiments.intervention: plant coupling cost q = sum_i q_i(s_i) + c * (sum of r rank-1 products) with r in {1,2,4}, c in {0.5, 2}; sweep lambda in {0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10}
experiments.control: same V passed through tanh(V/sd(V)) and through a rank-preserving quantile map to a Gaussian (non-exponential monotone transforms)
experiments.positive_control: purely additive q (c = 0): z must be exactly TT rank 1 and V TT rank 2; any deviation means the pipeline is broken
experiments.observable: max TT bond dimension at relative Frobenius tolerance 1e-6 (secondary 1e-3) for z, V, and controls
experiments.success_criterion: for c=0.5 and lambda >= 1, bond(z) <= bond(V) - 1 in >= 8/10 seeds for every r, AND bond(z) <= bond(tanh control) - 1 in >= 7/10 seeds, AND Spearman rho(r, bond(z)) >= 0.6 across seeds
experiments.failure_criterion: bond(z) >= bond(V) in >= 5/10 seeds at lambda >= 1, OR bond(z) is not lower than the tanh control in >= 5/10 seeds (exponential not special)
experiments.alternative_explanation: at large lambda z approaches constant, trivially low-rank; at small lambda z approaches a point mass
experiments.null_twin: entry-shuffled q (same histogram of cost values, factor structure destroyed): expect |bond(z) - bond(V)| <= 1 and both near full
experiments.why_this_implementation: an exact dense tensor with exact TT-SVD removes all learning noise; no ML model is needed
experiments.size: 4 state factors x 6 levels (1296 states), horizon 20, 10 seeds x 3 r x 2 c x 5 lambda = 300 solves
stupid_explanations: exp underflow to zero creating spurious low rank
lambda large makes z nearly constant
passive dynamics mixing to stationarity erasing structure over 20 steps

experiments.hypothesis: Required nonnegative rank R*(beta) of the Gibbs joint-action policy is non-monotone in beta and settles at the ground-state count for structured costs.
experiments.mechanism: mixture-of-products policies fitted by EM to Gibbs target exp(-beta C)/Z
experiments.intervention: coupled cost over 4 actuators x 3 levels (81 joint actions): ferromagnetic pairwise plus planted k-minima patterns, k in {2,3}; beta grid of 15 values log-spaced 0.1..30
experiments.positive_control: additive cost must give R*=1 at every beta
experiments.observable: R*(beta) = smallest R in 1..10 with KL(Gibbs || fit) < 0.01 nats (best of 5 restarts)
experiments.success_criterion: in >= 8/10 seeds: R* at beta=30 equals k, AND max over beta of R* exceeds R*(beta=30) by >= 1 (non-monotone), AND structured peak R* <= shuffled-null peak R* - 2
experiments.failure_criterion: R*(beta) monotone non-decreasing in >= 5/10 seeds, OR structured and shuffled peaks differ by < 2 in >= 5/10 seeds
experiments.alternative_explanation: EM local optima inflate R* at intermediate beta
experiments.null_twin: cost entries shuffled over the 81 joint actions, same histogram, one random global minimum typically
experiments.why_this_implementation: exact enumeration over 81 joint actions; mixture-of-products EM is the direct nonnegative CP of a distribution
experiments.size: 81 joint actions, R 1..10, 5 restarts, 15 betas, 10 seeds, 2 k values
stupid_explanations: non-monotonicity is generic interpolation between uniform and point mass
ground-state count trivially equals the planted k

experiments.hypothesis: With no explicit complexity penalty, evolved effective rank converges to W2's R*(beta) for the same cost.
experiments.mechanism: population of mixture-of-products genomes; mutations: add, delete, split, merge, perturb; fitness = -(E[C] - (1/beta) H)
experiments.intervention: costs from W2 at beta in {1, 3, 30}
experiments.control: same evolution with fitness = -E[C] only (no entropy term)
experiments.positive_control: additive cost must evolve effective rank 1 (+-0.5)
experiments.observable: effective rank = exp(entropy of mixture weights after merging components with total-variation < 0.05)
experiments.success_criterion: |mean effective rank over last 50 generations - R*(beta)| <= 0.75 in >= 7/10 seeds at each beta, AND shuffled-null effective rank differs from structured by >= 1.5 at beta=3
experiments.failure_criterion: effective rank drifts upward (slope > 0.005/generation over last 100 generations) in >= 5/10 seeds, OR deviates from R* by > 1.5
experiments.alternative_explanation: merge threshold produces convergence independent of selection
experiments.null_twin: shuffled cost from W2 with matched histogram

experiments.hypothesis: A Tucker subspace chosen from past goals' desirabilities beats a prediction-chosen subspace on in-span goals and loses on orthogonal goals.
experiments.mechanism: Galerkin-restricted linear Bellman solve within a K-dimensional per-mode Tucker subspace; policy u(s'|s) proportional to P(s'|s) z_hat(s')
experiments.intervention: subspace rule: (a) HOSVD of stacked training desirability tensor (goal x s1 x s2 x s3), (b) leading eigenvectors of passive per-mode transition, (c) random
experiments.control: rule (c) random subspace of same K
experiments.positive_control: test goal equal to a training goal: rule (a) regret < 1e-3 relative
experiments.observable: relative regret = (J(policy) - J*) / J* evaluated exactly
experiments.success_criterion: median regret (b)/(a) >= 2 on in-span goals AND median regret (a)/(b) >= 1.2 on orthogonal goals, in >= 7/10 seeds
experiments.failure_criterion: (a) not better than (b) by factor 2 in-span in >= 5/10 seeds, OR no reversal off-span in >= 5/10 seeds
experiments.alternative_explanation: subspace (a) simply has more energy in cost directions; crossover due to orthogonality by construction
experiments.null_twin: training desirabilities with mode fibers independently permuted per goal (spectra kept, shared factors destroyed)
experiments.why_this_implementation: exact small linear solves; the claim is about subspaces, so no learned network is required
experiments.size: 3 modes x 5 levels (125 states), K = 2 per mode, 10 training goals, 5 in-span + 5 orthogonal test goals, 10 seeds
